memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them. Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh." - Exodus 7:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After six chapters of objections, we finally read the simplest and best sentence: Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them.

No more arguing. No more faltering lips. Just obedience.

And then the detail that should stop every reader: Moses was eighty. Aaron was eighty-three. Moses' greatest work began at an age when most people are long finished.

He had spent forty years in a palace and forty years with sheep. From his own perspective, half his life had been wasted. God was not wasting any of it. The palace years taught him Egypt. The desert years taught him humility and the wilderness roads he would soon travel with a nation.

If you feel your best years are behind you, or that you started too late, look at this verse again. God's timetable is not ours. Caleb asked for a mountain at eighty-five. Anna was still serving in the temple in old age when she saw the Messiah (Lk 2:36-38).

You are not too old for God to use you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I written myself off because of my age or stage of life?
2. What has God been preparing in me during years I considered wasted?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that no season of my life is wasted with You. Use me now, at this age, for Your purposes. Amen.
